newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends firm on Iran-Germany row, technical.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends firm on Iran-Germany row, technical.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended firmer on Thursday, boosted by concerns about worsening relations between Europe and Iran and technical strength, dealers said.
May Brent closed 18 cents higher at $17.95 a barrel, 41 cents cents above a new nine-month low posted in earlier trade.
Brokers said the combination of a row between Germany and Iran over the killing of Kurdish exiles and the closure of the Houston ship channel drove prices higher.
"The Texas closure helped push U.S. gasoline higher but the other thing people have been looking at is the recall of European ambassadors from Iran," said a broker.

Brokers said news that the Houston channel was closed due to a capsized barge helped push NYMEX gasoline and heating oil through technical resistance, touching off stop-loss buying orders which lifted sentiment in London.
Earlier, Germany ordered four Iranian diplomats to leave the country after a Berlin court decision implicating Tehran in the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in a Berlin restaurant.
The European Union invited member countries to recall their ambassadors from Iran for consultations. Tehran responded by withdrawing its ambassador from Germany and expelling four German diplomats.
IPE gas oil futures ended weaker and towards the bottom of the day's range after the April contract expired with a whimper, dealers said.
Deliveries against the April contract, which expired at $160.25 a tonne, would total 1,072 lots or 107,200 tonne, an IPE official said.
May gas oil closed $3.75 lower at $160.50 a tonne.
